summary: At the end of a session the circulator signs a sworn statement that they saw each signature written.
realLife: State guides say the circulator must witness every signature, may not sign the sheet they carry, and must sign a notarized affidavit.
sources: Kansas Secretary of State, Candidate Petition Circulation Guide, 2020: https://kssos.org/Pubs/Elections/Guides/Candidate-Petition-Circulation-Guide.pdf
Common Cause Ohio, petition circulator FAQ, undated: https://commoncause.org/ohio/?p=484
inGame: petition sheet record: circulator affidavit and witnessed lines

turns.turn: The affidavit is signed and the sheet counts
turns.writesBack: the lines go to the clerk's count

turns.turn: The affidavit is wrong or missing
turns.writesBack: every line on the sheet is rejected
